text:
Evan: Heads up — canary NF4 rollout (canary-id c-2026-03-15-17) started showing oscillating kernel fallbacks and a GPU memory surge on prod-canary nodes. Throughput down ~45% on p99 windows.

Alex: saw a similar blip on staging earlier. flamegraph looks like kernel_select path toggling a lot. link: https://internal/perf/fg/18003

Evan: quick paste from the profiler: 
```
[2026-03-15T17:02:12Z] request=abcd step=0 latency=18ms -> 42ms
kernel_select: nf4_fast_v2 -> nf4_generic (range_check_fail)
KV cache allocs: +110MB per request spike
GPU mem: 12.1GB -> 18.9GB
throughput: 1200 req/s -> 680 req/s
```

Priya: calibration change note — the nf4 mapping introduced a new per-channel scale clamp (alpha_shift) in v2 which tightens range checks. If a weight's per-channel scale moves slightly we get the range_check_fail and the runtime falls back to generic kernel that is not quantization-optimized. That fallback path triggers extra temp buffers and kills batching.

Jorge: infra metrics: observed increased fragmentation in KV cache allocator around the same time window. GPU allocator freed fewer large blocks, leading to more small allocs; combined with generic kernel extra buffers -> OOM margin shrink and mem spike.

Tina: alert from perf-bot showed 4 concurrent canary nodes crossing latency SLO. We throttled external traffic but internal load still caused degradations.

perf-bot: ALERT: canary c-2026-03-15-17 - p99 latency +104% vs baseline; kernel_fallback_rate 31% (baseline 2%); mem_spike_detected = true.

Evan: immediate ask — can we force the old kernel on canary to validate? Kernel override env var exists: REDWOOD_KERNEL_FORCE=nf4_fast_v1.

Alex: I pushed a small change to runtime that exposes per-request debug flags, can set REDWOOD_DEBUG_KERNEL_DECISIONS=1 to log why a selection happened. Recommend flip force to v1 for canary and collect logs for ~15m.

Priya: longer term: need to re-run calibration sweep with the new quantization range relaxations per-layer: try clip_threshold = [1.05,1.1] and re-evaluate. Also add a fallback budget so generic_fallbacks per-second are rate-limited to avoid allocator thrash.

Jorge: rolling kernel-force to canary now (c-2026-03-15-17 -> c-2026-03-15-17a). infra-bot: deploy triggered.

infra-bot: deploy event: user=jorge service=runtime-canary target=c-2026-03-15-17a commit=abc123 force_kernel=nf4_fast_v1

Evan: after the kernel-force, p95/p99 dropped back near baseline and fallback_rate went to <3%. KV cache allocs normalized. Still want to collect full debug logs and flamegraphs.

Alex: next steps: 1) collect DEBUG_KERNEL_DECISIONS logs on canary for 1h, 2) run calibration sweep on a clone of canary with new clamp params, 3) add a gating check in rollout pipeline: if kernel_fallback_rate > 5% within first 30m, auto-pause rollout.

Priya: I'll own the calibration sweep and produce a short report with per-layer scale distributions + suggested clip thresholds. Will also run a small synthetic workload to validate batching behavior since fallback kills batch coalescing.

Tina: I'll update ops runbook with the immediate mitigation steps and add a quickplaybook for forcing kernels and monitoring alloc heatmaps.

Evan: thanks — agreed plan. Let's keep this thread for debug outputs only. Post the debug logs and flamegraphs as links here when available.
